name: French Revolution
hook: Bastille, guillotine and Terror: the upheaval that reshaped France and its fiction.

facts.label: the storming of the Bastille
facts.statement: The French Revolution began in 1789; the storming of the Bastille prison on July 14 is its most famous event.

facts.label: the Reign of Terror
facts.statement: The Reign of Terror was the Revolution's bloody phase, ended by Robespierre's overthrow and execution in 1794.

facts.label: the guillotine
facts.statement: The guillotine stood in the Place de la Concorde, the largest square in Paris, during the Revolution.

facts.label: Jean-Paul Marat
facts.statement: Jean-Paul Marat was stabbed to death in his bath by Charlotte Corday in 1793.

facts.label: A Tale of Two Cities
facts.statement: Charles Dickens set A Tale of Two Cities in Paris and London during the French Revolution; it was published in 1859.

facts.label: The Scarlet Pimpernel
facts.statement: In The Scarlet Pimpernel, Percy Blakeney uses a red pimpernel flower as his secret identity during the Revolution.

facts.label: Napoleon Bonaparte
facts.statement: Napoleon seized control of the Directory on November 9, 1799, ending the French Revolution.
